job.value: decide whether this card at this price is worth buying

arrivedFrom.value: a listing card on the TCG SERP

questions.title: The screen's job is clear from the first screen
questions.why: Large card photo, 'Pikachu E3 Stamp — Base Set 58/102 (Near Mint)' and 'S$41' make it a listing page.

questions.title: The action that does the job stands out most
questions.why: 'Buy' is the one filled red button in the fixed bottom bar.

questions.title: Every label says what happens when tapped
questions.why: 'Price is typical >' carries a chevron so it reads as a link to more price detail; 'Add to cart' and 'Buy' are explicit.

questions.title: No terms this user wouldn't know
questions.why: 'Near Mint', 'Base', 'E3 Stamp', 'Rarity' are TCG terms this buyer knows, and 'Condition' has an info icon.

questions.title: Only asks what this user can decide at this stage
questions.why: Nothing is asked beyond buy / add to cart / like.

questions.title: Advanced detail is tucked away
questions.why: Price history sits behind the 'Price is typical' chip rather than on the page.

questions.title: Everything fits this stage and this user
questions.why: Buyer Protection tag, details and price signal all serve a buyer deciding.

questions.title: Little reading needed to act
questions.why: Price, the price chip and short label/value detail rows carry the decision.
